definition: A generative probabilistic model used for topic modeling, where each document is modeled as a mixture of latent topics and each topic as a distribution over words.
details: LDA was one of the most influential topic modeling techniques in the pre-deep-learning era of NLP, and remains a useful baseline for unsupervised text analysis.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Think of it this way: A generative probabilistic model used for topic modeling, where each document is modeled as a mixture of latent topics and each topic as a distribution over words. And here is the clever part: LDA was one of the most influential topic modeling techniques in the pre-deep-learning era of NLP, and remains a useful baseline for unsupervised text analysis. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Latent Dirichlet Allocation — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
